text:
SRE Pager: [INCIDENT] CeruleanCorp (vpc-cerulean-prod) elevated 5xx and token latency on model family 'redwood-7b' in dedicated pool dc-eu-2. Error rate +45% over 5m. Paging @Matt S @Sam R @Kara O :rotating_light:

Matt S: ack — I'm on. joining call now, switching pager to active. Can someone drop the top-level logs?

Sam R: looking. initial read: we’re seeing repeated QuantFallback exceptions on the v3-quant variant, then routing tried to autoswap to 'redwood-7b-safe-v2' but the tenant routing table didn’t match the fallback policy (tenant has explicit model alias).

Matt S: thanks. impact? are customer requests failing or just slower?

SRE Pager: customer-facing inference calls returning 500s intermittently (about 12% of requests) and p95 token latency ~2.3s. Cerulean reports increased error surface in their app.

Kara O: cerulean-support (external) notified via email, opening a high-priority status note. I'll draft a short status update for their CS team once we have mitigation plan.

Sam R: hypothesis: quantized variant instability under concurrent KV-cache eviction + aggressive batching. We can mitigate by pinning Cerulean's tenant to 'redwood-7b-safe-v2' (non-quant) and temporarily lowering max_concurrency to avoid queue explosion.

Alex P: if we pin, make sure to set a fallback TTL so the pin is explicit and reversible. Also add a short circuit to prevent autoswap mesh from undoing the pin.

Matt S: plan: 1) patch tenant routing to pin model -> redwood-7b-safe-v2 2) lower concurrency for their pool to 80% of current 3) monitor metrics for 15m 4) update customer. I'll execute routing patch now.

Matt S: running command to patch routing:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/tenants/cerulean-prod/routing \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"pin_model":"redwood-7b-safe-v2","pin_ttl":"30m","disable_autoswap":true}'
```

SRE Pager: deploy bot: routing-change queued by Matt S — change-id rc-8792.

Matt S: applied rc-8792, confirmed config shows pin_model=redwood-7b-safe-v2, ttl=30m, disable_autoswap=true. Patching pool concurrency now.

Matt S: set pool dc-eu-2 concurrency to 80% -> command: `rbctl pools update dc-eu-2 --concurrency 0.8` -> applied.

Sam R: watching metrics: error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% in the last 2 mins, p95 latency down to 1.1s. Nice.

Kara O: sending status to Cerulean now: "We have pinned your tenant to a safe model variant and applied temporary concurrency limits. We expect reduced errors within 15 minutes. We'll follow up with a root cause and ETA for rollback."

Lina C: create follow-up ticket to evaluate whether the safe variant maintains quality for Cerulean workload (prompt evals) and to plan a canary reintroduction of quant variant with throttled traffic. Assign to eng-runtime.

Matt S: ticket created: INC-9712-followup, assigned to Sam R, due EOD.

Alex P: add runbook note: when pinning, always set TTL + disable_autoswap; document exact change-id and link to pool metrics.

Sam R: agree. I'll leave monitoring alerts with a 10m quiet window and add regression watch on outputs. If error rate creeps back above 5%, we'll escalate to full rollback and tenant isolation.

Matt S: handing off active watch to Alex P in 30m. @Kara O can you stay on customer comms until next update?

Kara O: yes, I'll stay on it and update Cerulean support every 10m.

SRE Pager: incident status: mitigation applied, customer impact reduced. On-call handoff planned in ~30m.

Alex P: taking over watch in 30m. If anything spikes, page me and tag @Sam R and @Matt S.

Matt S: thanks team. I'll add a short postmortem stub while this is fresh.

Kara O: noted. I'll include the customer-facing timeline in the status doc. :white_check_mark:
